'''Urszula Alicja Foryś''' (born 1965 in Warsaw, Poland) is a Polish mathematician specializing in applied mathematics, mathematical biology, and biomedical engineering. She is a professor at the [[University of Warsaw]] and is known for her research on mathematical modeling of cancer therapy and biological dynamical systems. Foryś has supervised numerous doctoral students, including [[Jan Poleszczuk]], and is a laureate of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]]'s Hugo Steinhaus Award (2025). She is also an accomplished powerlifting athlete.

== Early life and education ==
Foryś attended Primary School No. 1 and Jan Śniadecki High School XXX in Warsaw. In 1989 she received a Master of Science degree with honours in applied mathematics from the [[University of Warsaw]]'s Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Mechanics (MIM), under the supervision of [[Wiesław Szlenk]]. She completed her Ph.D. in 1996 with the dissertation ''Global analysis of the Marczuk model for the immune organism and the immunodeficient organism'', supervised by Szlenk and, following his death, by [[:pl:Andrzej Palczewski|Andrzej Palczewski]].<ref name="UAFinMGP">{{Cite web |title=Urszula Forys - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=242370 |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu}}</ref>

In 2007, she received her habilitation (D.Sc.) in biocybernetics and biomedical engineering from the [[:pl:Instytut Biocybernetyki i Inżynierii Biomedycznej im. Macieja Nałęcza Polskiej Akademii Nauk|Nałęcz Institute of Biocybernetics and Biomedical Engineering]], [[Polish Academy of Sciences]], for the dissertation ''Mathematical modelling of tumour development taking into account various stages of tumour growth''. On 20 June 2018, the President of the Republic of Poland conferred on her the title of professor of mathematical sciences.<ref>{{cite web |title=Resolution of the President of the Republic of Poland of 20 June 2018, No. 115.8.2018 |url=https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/download.xsp/WMP20180000748/O/M20180748.pdf |website=Monitor Polski |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Since 1989 Foryś has worked at the Institute of Applied Mathematics and Mechanics (MIM), [[University of Warsaw]], where she advanced from junior assistant to full professor (2019). She currently leads the Division of Biomathematics and Game Theory, which she helped establish in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zakład Biomatematyki i Teorii Gier – MIM UW |url=https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/zaklady/biomatematyki-i-teorii-gier |website=University of Warsaw |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

She has held visiting positions at the [[China University of Geosciences (Wuhan)|China University of Geosciences]] in Wuhan (2011–2014) and has collaborated with numerous research centers, including the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]], the Institute for Medical Biomathematics in [[Bene Atarot]], [[Israel]], and the [[University of Dundee]] in Scotland. She was also a member of the Cooperation Group "Multiscale Modeling of Tumor Initiation, Growth and Progression" at the Center for Interdisciplinary Research (ZiF) of [[Bielefeld University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Cooperation Group – Multiscale Modeling of Tumor Initiation, Growth and Progression |url=https://www.uni-bielefeld.de/(en)/ZiF/FG/2018Multiscale/ |website=Bielefeld University |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

In 2019–2020 she carried out research at the Institute for Medical Biomathematics (Israel) under the Bekker Programme of the [[Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange]] (NAWA).<ref>{{cite web |title=NAWA Bekker Programme – Urszula Foryś |url=https://nawa.gov.pl/en/nawa-programmes/the-bekker-programme |website=Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

== Research ==
Foryś's research focuses on applications of finite- and infinite-dimensional dynamical systems to biomedicine, ecology, and social sciences. Her scientific output includes about 100 research papers indexed in [[MathSciNet]] and [[zbMATH]], as well as educational and outreach publications. She is the author of the textbook ''Matematyka w biologii'' (''Mathematics in Biology'', WNT, 2005),<ref>{{cite book |last=Foryś |first=Urszula |title=Matematyka w biologii |publisher=Wydawnictwa Naukowo-Techniczne |location=Warsaw |year=2005 |isbn=83-204-3123-9}}</ref> and the co-translator (with [[Marek Bodnar]]) of James D. Murray's ''Mathematical Biology I: An Introduction'' into Polish (PWN, 2006).<ref>{{cite book |last=Murray |first=James D. |title=Mathematical Biology: An Introduction |edition=3rd |publisher=Springer |year=2002 |translator=Urszula Foryś, Marek Bodnar |isbn=978-0-387-22437-4}}</ref>

She has collaborated with international teams on cancer therapy modeling, including studies on CAR-T cell therapy for glioblastoma<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Szafrańska-Łęczycka |first1=Magdalena |last2=Szymańska |first2=Zuzanna |last3=Piotrowska |first3=Monika J. |last4=Bodnar |first4=Marek |last5=Foryś |first5=Urszula |title=CAR-T cell therapy for glioblastoma: insight from mathematical modeling |journal=Frontiers in Immunology |year=2025 |volume=16 |article-number=1563829 |doi=10.3389/fimmu.2025.1563829 |doi-access=free |pmid=40607424 |pmc=12213547 }}</ref> and hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treatment.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Foryś |first1=Urszula |last2=Nahshony |first2=Alon |last3=Elishmereni |first3=Moran |title=Mathematical model of hormone sensitive prostate cancer treatment using leuprolide: A small step towards personalization |journal=PLOS ONE |year=2022 |volume=17 |issue=2 |article-number=e0263648 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0263648 |doi-access=free |pmid=35167616 |pmc=8846544 |bibcode=2022PLoSO..1763648F }}</ref>

Her doctoral students include [[Jan Poleszczuk|Jan Poleszczuk (2014,2015)]], [[:pl:Piotr Bajger|Piotr Bajger (2021)]], and [[:pl:Marcin Choinski|Marcin Choinski(2022)]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ludzie Nauki – Urszula Foryś |url=https://ludzie.nauka.gov.pl/ln/profiles/urszula.fory%C5%9B.fFKFosL28pq |website=Ludzie Nauki |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

== Professional and community service ==
Foryś is a founding member of the [https://www.esmtb.org/ European Society for Mathematical and Theoretical Biology] (ESMTB)<ref name="ESMTB">{{cite web
 |title = European Society for Mathematical and Theoretical Biology – History
 |url = https://www.esmtb.org/
 |publisher = ESMTB
 |language = en
 |access-date = 21 October 2025
}}</ref> and participated in the first European Conference on Mathematics Applied to Biology and Medicine (L'Alpe d'Huez, 1991). She has served in leadership roles within the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] (PTM), including as president of its Warsaw Branch (2019–2023) and vice-president (2023–2025). She is also an editor of ''Mathematica Applicanda'' and organized the exhibition *On Mathematics and Mathematicians* in the Senate of Poland (2019).<ref>{{cite web |title=Polish Mathematical Society – Warsaw Branch |url=https://ptm.org.pl/ |website=PTM |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

She co-founded and serves as vice-president of the [https://pwm.ptm.org.pl/ Polish Women in Mathematics Association]([[:pl:Polskie_Towarzystwo_Kobiet_w_Matematyce|PTKwM]]) since 2016,<ref>{{cite web |title=Polish Women in Mathematics – About us |url=https://pwm.ptm.org.pl/ |website=PTKwM |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref> and since 2024 has been a member of the Commission on Mathematical Applications of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]. She also chairs the Scientific Committee of the National Conference on Mathematical Applications in Biology and Medicine (KKZMBM).<ref>{{cite web |title=KKZMBM – National Conference on Mathematical Applications in Biology and Medicine |url=https://kkzmbm.ptm.org.pl/ |website=Polish Mathematical Society |access-date=21 October 2025}}</ref>

== Sports career ==
Outside academia, Foryś is an experienced powerlifter, representing TKKF Herkules Warszawa. She is a multiple Polish champion, European Masters II Champion (2015), and World Vice-Champion Masters III (2025).<ref>{{cite web |title=International Powerlifting Federation – 2025 Bench Press Championships, Drammen |url=https://www.powerlifting.sport/championships/results/2025/world-open-sub-juniors-juniors-masters-classic-equipped-bench-press-championships-2025 |website=IPF |access-date=23 October 2025}}</ref>
